clue.text: Concise version of two hundred tunics

indicators.note: a version of something is a reworking of it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two hundred is CC

explanation.surface: A tailor's pared-down rendering of an order for two hundred tunics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' asks for CC plus TUNICS to be rearranged; the three Cs are the giveaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe expression that is brief and to the point.

clue.text: Educational establishment which confuses cool and rash youth after a short time

indicators.note: after puts the jumbled letters behind the word for a short time

parts.note: a second is a brief moment

indicators.note: something that confuses mixes things up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Y is a standard abbreviation for youth or young, as in YHA, Youth Hostels Association

explanation.surface: A school where cool and impetuous teenagers mingle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confuses' shuffles COOL, RASH and Y into ARYSCHOOL; 'after' puts that behind SECOND.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary school is a school for pupils from about eleven to eighteen.

clue.text: Triumphs for birds

definitions.meaning: exults or boasts over a victory
large black birds of the genus Corvus

explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to exult over a victory, and crows are also black birds.

clue.text: Those breathing have slain her

indicators.note: a loose signal: the following words are to be had, that is rearranged, into the answer

explanation.surface: A grim accusation that the living have killed a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of SLAIN HER rearrange; 'have' is a very loose anagram signal, typical of older puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhaler is literally one who breathes in.

clue.text: Bit of food which is heartily strange

definitions.text: Bit of food which is heartily strange

parts.words: Bit of food which is heartily strange
parts.note: the small piece of bread has at its heart a word meaning odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: A morsel that seems thoroughly peculiar.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the first and last letters and you are left with RUM, British slang for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumb is a tiny fragment of bread or cake.

clue.text: A journalist journeyed back without it

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the reversed word sits round the other piece
travelled back tells us the word for journeyed is read in reverse

parts.note: rode means journeyed, on horseback

explanation.surface: A reporter makes a return trip and forgets to take something along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RODE into EDOR; 'without' means outside, so EDOR is split round IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper editor is one kind of journalist, the one in charge of the paper's content.

clue.text: Get rid of the pollutant, making part of London all right at heart

definitions.text: Get rid of the pollutant, making part of London all right at heart

parts.words: Get rid of the pollutant, making part of London all right at heart
parts.note: to remove carbon deposits; the middle of the word is EC, the City of London postcode, followed by a word for all right

explanation.surface: A call to clean up smog and so make the city healthy at its core.
explanation.walkthrough: Its heart is EC, the postal district of the City of London, plus OK.
explanation.definitionFit: To decoke an engine is to remove the carbon deposits that build up inside it.

clue.text: Confused tories are about to make a mistake and practise intimidation

indicators.note: being about something means surrounding it, so the jumbled letters go round the next piece
confused means jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Muddled Conservatives are on the verge of a blunder and bullying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' turns TORIES into TORISE; 'are about' wraps it round ERR. Tories are Britain's Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: To terrorise is to coerce by threats and fear, which is intimidation.

clue.text: Dressing don when about to act nothing up in spirit

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the two words go round the next piece

parts.note: robing is putting on robes, dressing
a don is a university teacher, also called a fellow of a college

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: to do is to act
O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A university lecturer puts on his gown, about to perform nothing in particular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DO plus O into OOD; 'about' sets it between ROBING and FELLOW. A don is an Oxbridge academic.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Goodfellow is another name for Puck, the mischievous sprite of English folklore.

clue.text: Engaged although shy

definitions.meaning: booked in advance, as a table

explanation.surface: Someone is betrothed despite being timid.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means booked for someone and also quiet and reticent in manner.

clue.text: Change one's home into a kind of restaurant

parts.note: to chop is to change, as in the phrase chop and change
a house is a home

explanation.surface: Someone converts their home into an eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: CHOP for change comes from the idiom 'chop and change', to keep switching about.
explanation.definitionFit: A chophouse is an old-fashioned restaurant serving steaks and cutlets.

clue.text: If this language lacked an article it would provide a key for schoolchildren

definitions.text: If this language lacked an article it would provide a key for schoolchildren

parts.words: If this language lacked an article it would provide a key for schoolchildren
parts.note: the language's name, minus the indefinite article A, leaves a word for a pupil's illicit translation aid

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a language that would become a schoolroom cheat sheet if shorn of a word.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A (an article) out of the language's name and you get CRIB, a key or translation that schoolchildren copy from.
explanation.definitionFit: Carib is the language of the indigenous Caribbean people of the Lesser Antilles.

clue.text: Organ's sound

definitions.meaning: belonging to the nose, the organ of smell
a speech sound made through the nose, like m or n

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to the nose, and as a noun it names a sound produced through the nostrils.

clue.text: Analysis needed for bad state

definitions.meaning: a detailed itemised account, as of costs

explanation.surface: An examination needed because things have deteriorated.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both an itemised analysis of figures and a collapse in health or function.

clue.text: Lotion which the following course possesses

parts.note: afters is British slang for pudding, the course that follows the main one
to have is to possess

explanation.surface: A diner wonders which lotion the next course of the meal holds.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is everyday British for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a scented lotion applied to the face after a shave.

clue.text: Transport for which a drawback arises after it goes to marshy ground

indicators.note: after places the reversed word behind the earlier pieces

parts.note: a bog is marshy ground

indicators.note: in a down clue arising reads from bottom to top, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a snag is a drawback

explanation.surface: A vehicle that runs into trouble once it heads onto swampy land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arises' turns SNAG into GANS, which goes after TO and BOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Toboggans are sleds used to carry people over snow.

clue.text: It is not simple to give support to such a book

parts.note: hard means difficult, not simple
to back is to support

explanation.surface: Endorsing this kind of volume is no easy matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardback is a book bound in stiff covers.

clue.text: Should you be going back to the party with this dog?

indicators.note: going back tells us the word meaning should you is read in reverse

parts.note: should you go means if you go
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A host asks whether you will bring this dog when you return to the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Should you' is IF, which 'be going back' turns into FI; DO, a party, follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Fido is the stock name for a pet dog.

clue.text: Critic concerned with the television audience

parts.note: re means concerning, as in business letters
a viewer is a member of the television audience

explanation.surface: A critic who cares about the people watching TV.
explanation.definitionFit: A reviewer writes critical assessments of books, plays or films.

clue.text: One of these louts is a backward child

definitions.text: One of these louts is a backward child

parts.words: One of these louts is a backward child
parts.note: the singular word for a lout is a word for a male child written back to front, as in back slang

explanation.surface: A remark that a hooligan is just a slow-witted kid.
explanation.walkthrough: The singular is BOY spelt backwards, as in Victorian back slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Yobs are loutish, aggressive young men.

clue.text: Advance position held for game with teacher

parts.note: bridge is a card game
the head is the headteacher of a school

explanation.surface: A military foothold is gained for a match against a schoolmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: HEAD is the British shorthand for a headteacher or headmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridgehead is a forward position held by an army in enemy territory, especially across a river.

clue.text: Street philosopher is one who endures

parts.note: A. J. Ayer was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: A thinker on the street keeps going.
explanation.walkthrough: A. J. Ayer was a well-known twentieth-century British philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: A stayer is a horse or person with stamina, able to keep going.

clue.text: It is conceivable that it comes between an unimportant member and one who is competent

indicators.note: something that comes between two others is placed inside their pair

parts.note: a cog is a small, unimportant member of a machine or organisation
able means competent

explanation.surface: A claim that something might slip between a minor player and a skilled one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes between' puts IT inside the pair COG and ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something that can be thought of or imagined.

clue.text: Join up in turn when rolling along

indicators.note: in signals that the letters lie inside the following words

explanation.surface: Recruits fall in, one after another, as the column rolls on.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'when rolling': whEN ROLling.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to sign on as a member, such as joining the army.

clue.text: Moisten, but reduced in this person after one

indicators.note: after places the next piece behind the word for one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in sets the shortened word inside the word for this person

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as me

indicators.note: reduced means the word but loses its final letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to dampen something, with a grumbling but trailing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts BUT to BU; 'in' places it inside ME, and 'after' puts the lot after I.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue is to soak or saturate, so moisten is its older literal sense.

clue.text: An old conductor spent a morning under this tree

indicators.note: spent means used up, so the conductor loses that part

parts.note: Sir Thomas Beecham was a famous British conductor
AM stands for ante meridiem, morning

explanation.surface: A famous conductor passed a morning beneath a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Thomas Beecham was a celebrated British conductor; 'spent' removes AM from his name.
explanation.definitionFit: The beech is a broad-leaved tree with smooth grey bark.

clue.text: Female part which makes madame lose her head

indicators.note: losing her head means the name drops its first letter

parts.note: Madame Bovary is the heroine of Flaubert's novel

explanation.surface: A description of a lady being beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madame' points to Flaubert's Madame Bovary; 'lose her head' drops the B.
explanation.definitionFit: The ovary is the female reproductive organ that produces eggs.

clue.text: Carry instrument of torture for gymnastic exercise

parts.note: to cart is to carry
the wheel was a medieval instrument of torture on which victims were broken

explanation.surface: Someone hauls a torture device into the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartwheel is a sideways handspring with arms and legs outstretched.

clue.text: Period for splendour

definitions.meaning: a span of five years, also spelt lustrum

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a five-year span and radiant brilliance or glory.

clue.text: Women's Institute lecher reforming verse

indicators.note: reforming means forming anew, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: WI stands for the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women

explanation.surface: The Women's Institute takes a lecher in hand and reforms him, with poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI, the Women's Institute, is a British organisation of women's community groups.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerihew is a short comic biographical poem of four lines, named after E. Clerihew Bentley.
